question: The cost price of an item is ₹150, and it is sold for ₹135. What is the percentage loss?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss = CP − SP = 150 − 135 = 15

Loss % = (Loss / CP) × 100

Loss % = (15 / 150) × 100 = 10%

In decimal form, 10% = 10/100 = 0.1

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹150

Selling Price (SP) = ₹135

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Cost Price − Selling Price<
